prize_parts.citation: for the development of ionizable lipid nanoparticles as carriers for nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a molecular design achievement rooted in lipid self-assembly: lipids that are neutral at physiological pH and charged in the acidic endosome, formulated through controlled assembly and rapid mixing, with non-bilayer phase propensity and membrane fusion enabling cargo release. The resulting platform delivered siRNA (Onpattro) and mRNA vaccines at a scale of billions of doses, has been independently reproduced with many lipid designs, and is the open carrier half of a story whose cargo half was recognised by the 2023 Medicine prize. The scientific principle (pKa-tuned lipids, assembly and endosomal escape) is clear and chemically rational, and the maturity is not in question. Among the shortlisted topics it combines the strongest evidence of impact with the cleanest chemical concept.
statement.case_against: Credit is crowded and partly entangled with patents and with several overlapping groups: Anderson and Langer (combinatorial lipidoids), MacLachlan (clinical translation), and the Vancouver group's own members. Any three-person cut is exclusionary, and the question of who invented the decisive ionizable lipid versus the formulation process is not fully settled. A further objection is that the achievement is as much pharmaceutical engineering as fundamental chemistry, and that the recent Medicine prize might be judged to have already covered the mRNA vaccine territory.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks prime editing (B061) first, as a designed protein and RNA invention distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize, but also puts B035 second and proposes a compact Cullis-Anderson pairing.
responses.response: I agree that B035 belongs near the top, but I would not narrow it to Cullis and Anderson. Anderson's lipidoid work came later and followed a different route, and a pair would drop Hope and Madden, who did the early work on pH-dependent lipid behaviour and formulation. I also differ on prime editing: it is only about seven years old and, like base editing, sits close to the 2020 prize, so I think it is early in a way that B035 is not.

responses.point: Aili ranks targeted protein degradation (B063) first as a conceptually original new modality, and puts B035 second, noting that the three-person cut for B063 is contestable.
responses.response: I take the conceptual originality of PROTACs and the cereblon story seriously, and I keep B063 as my first alternative. My reservation is maturity and attribution: no degrader is approved yet, and eight credited names spread over PROTAC design, cereblon biology and VHL chemistry make a clean three-person citation hard. B035 has the opposite profile, with settled clinical proof and a narrower core group, so I would give it priority this year while accepting that B063 may be the next in line.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks proton-coupled electron transfer (B025) first on conceptual grounds, and regards biomolecular condensates (B046) as probably premature because physiological relevance is contested.
responses.response: I agree with him on B046: the concept is influential, but the evidence that many reported condensates are true functional liquids in vivo is still debated, and I made the same point in my own ranking. I disagree somewhat on B025, which I did not rank. The physical principle is sound, but a prize there would reward a unifying theory more than a single decisive invention, and the split among Mayer, Hammes-Schiffer, Nocera and Meyer is hard to draw. I would want to hear how he would divide credit.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B063 first and B035 second, with Cullis, Hope and Anderson, and notes that the LNP configuration is crowded and patent-entangled.
responses.response: We agree on the carrier chemistry and on its timeliness after the 2023 Medicine prize, so the open question is the trio. I prefer Cullis, Hope and Madden because they built the ionizable-lipid and formulation science from the beginning, and Anderson's contribution came later through lipidoids. I accept that this choice is debatable and that the patent history should not decide it; the committee should rely on the primary literature.

uncertainties: Who should hold the third place in B035: Madden (early lipid and formulation work) or Anderson (lipidoid discovery), and whether Langer or MacLachlan has a stronger claim.
Whether the committee regards ionizable LNP delivery as primarily chemistry rather than pharmaceutical technology, after the 2023 Medicine prize.
Whether approval of the first degrader drug would move B063 ahead of B035 in later rounds.
Whether the physiological case for biomolecular condensates (B046) will be settled soon enough to treat the field as mature.
statement.conflict_note: No specific personal or institutional conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My research on lipid self-assembly, membrane biophysics and amyloid is close to B035 and B046 in subject matter, and I work in the same Lund department as colleagues on the committee, but I have no stated tie to any credited candidate. I will declare any collaboration or prior association with candidates if one is found.
